newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rep moves to block Wake Island nuclear dump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rep moves to block Wake Island nuclear dump.

text.p: A U.S. lawmaker from Hawaii Tuesday introduced a resolution to block an effort by private investors to build a radioactive waste dump on Wake Island in the Pacific.
Democratic Rep. Neil Abercrombie said his resolution would express the "sense of Congress in opposition to nuclear waste storage on any U.S. territory or possession," such as Wake Island.

Representatives from Nuclear Disarmament Services and an associate firm U.S. Fuel and Security Inc were in Washington this week pushing their plan to build a facility at Wake Island to hold containers of waste nuclear fuel.

The backers contended this would be the safest way to keep the material -- largely from the United States and Russia -- from hands of terrorists and rogue governments that could use the radioactive waste to produce nuclear weapons.

While the Clinton administration is grappling with where to safely and permamently dispose of nuclear waste, the administration in May said it had no interest in the private investors' plan. "My resolution is a preemptive strike against those who would turn the Pacific into a radioactive dumping ground," Abercrombie said in a statement.
